evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:280-311 — execute_workflow() unconditionally `tokio::spawn`s a detached WorkflowExecutorTask::run per workflow with NO concurrency gate: no Semaphore permit is acquired before the spawn and none is held inside the task. The spawned task immediately calls acquire_with_rls (via run -> rls_conn) to grab a DB connection.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:186,198 — the config exposes `pub max_concurrent_executions: usize` (default 10), documented as the execution concurrency cap, but a repo-wide grep (`Semaphore|acquire_owned|permit|max_concurrent_executions`) across backend/servers/api-server/src finds the field is referenced ONLY at its definition and default — it is never read to build a Semaphore or otherwise enforced. The cap is dead config.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:315-380 — handle_event() loops over every workflow returned by list_by_trigger_type for an event and calls execute_workflow (one detached spawn each) with no batch bound. Impact: a burst of matching trigger events (or one event matching many workflows) spawns unbounded concurrent executions, each acquiring an RLS DB connection — a resource-exhaustion / pool-starvation path, and the documented `max_concurrent_executions` limit silently does nothing. Landable backend-only fix: build a `tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(config.max_concurrent_executions)` once in the executor, `acquire_owned()` a permit before `tokio::spawn`, and move the permit into the task so it is held for the execution lifetime (or bound handle_event's per-event fan-out). Reachability of the spawn is certain (handle_event -> execute_workflow -> tokio::spawn); kept at medium because triggering actual pool exhaustion depends on event/workflow volume at runtime, which static analysis cannot execute.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:216 — `// TODO: Date proximity` marks an unimplemented scoring factor in run_payment_matcher's per-invoice confidence loop (accounting.rs:182-226). The matcher accumulates variable-symbol (0.8), amount (0.15 exact / 0.05 partial) and counterparty-IBAN (0.05) signals and compares against the 0.5 auto-suggest threshold, but the intended date-proximity corroboration (statement-line date vs invoice due/issue date) is never computed.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:198-214,228-234 — because the date signal is absent, the tie-breaker set for VS-sharing invoices relies solely on amount + IBAN. For a tenant's recurring monthly invoices that share a variable symbol and amount (the common case for rent), nothing date-aware promotes the invoice whose period actually matches the payment date, so genuinely-equal-scoring candidates are all surfaced for manual resolution. Impact: weaker auto-reconciliation than FR-16.8 designs for -> more manual bank-line matching work. Landable backend-only fix: implement the date-proximity branch (e.g. small positive weight when |line.value_date - invoice.due_date| is within a window), keeping the clamped-to-1.0 confidence invariant at accounting.rs:221. Low severity (quality/completeness, not a crash).

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:155,193,200,202,212 — run_payment_matcher parses constant decimal weights with `Decimal::from_str("0.5").unwrap()` (threshold) and `Decimal::from_str("0.8"|"0.15"|"0.05").unwrap()` (confidence weights). The weight parses at 193/200/202/212 sit inside the `for invoice in &open_invoices` loop (accounting.rs:182-226), so a known-valid literal is re-parsed on every (line x invoice) pair.
